3: /*
4:  * A framework for writing general tests.
5:  *
6:  * A general test typically consists of two parts, the setup part and the
7:  * test part. The setup part contains setup functions that set up the context
8:  * for the subsequent tests to run. The setup functions cannot fail, and if they
9:  * do, execution is aborted because the subsequent tests will not work as
10:  * expected either. The test functions, on the other hand, can fail, and if they
11:  * do, they are reported as test failures.
12:  *
13:  * The framework provides basic utilities for writing general tests:
14:  *
15:  *  - To define a setup function or a test function, FN_SETUP() or FN_TEST() can
16:  * be used. These functions are automatically executed in the order of their
17:  * definition. Note that the order of execution is _not_ related to whether a
18:  * function is a setup function or a test function.
19:  *
20:  *  - Within a setup function, CHECK() can be used to write a setup expression
21:  * that must succeed. If the expression fails, a fatal error will be reported
22:  * and the execution will be aborted.
23:  *
24:  *  - Within a test function, TEST_SUCC() can be used to write a test expression
25:  * that should succeed. If the expression fails, a test failure will be reported
26:  * but the execution will continue.
27:  *
28:  *  - The number of successful and failed tests is tracked. When a test function

30:  * failures. The program will exit with a non-zero code if and only if there is
31:  * at least one test failure.
32:  */

source: book/src/to-contribute/coding-guidelines/for-maintainability/rust-specific/crates-and-modules.md#narrow-visibility

### Default to the narrowest visibility (`narrow-visibility`) {#narrow-visibility}

Start private,
then widen to `pub(super)`, `pub(crate)`, or `pub`
only when an actual external consumer requires it.

```rust
// Good — restricted to the parent module
pub(super) static I8042_CONTROLLER:
    Once<SpinLock<I8042Controller, LocalIrqDisabled>> = Once::new();

pub(super) fn init() -> Result<(), I8042ControllerError> {
    // ...
}

// Bad — unnecessarily wide
pub static I8042_CONTROLLER: ...
```

Inside the `aster-kernel` crate, `pub(crate)` and `pub` are equivalent,
as the crate has no downstream consumers.
Prefer the shorter `pub`.

See also:
PR [#2951](https://github.com/asterinas/asterinas/pull/2951),
[#2605](https://github.com/asterinas/asterinas/pull/2605#discussion_r2720506912),
and [#3154](https://github.com/asterinas/asterinas/pull/3154#discussion_r3100905375).
